Container.Name: Suricata-Proxy-IDS
Container.Overview: Passive Suricata IDS with integrated configuration initialization, ET Open updates and log rotation. Select the exact reverse proxy container under Network Type and set its capture interface and your internal networks below. Start the proxy first. Recreate this sensor after the proxy is recreated. Use the companion EveBox template to view alerts. This image must first be published through the repository workflow; see README.

Config.Name: Capture interface
Config.Description: Interface inside the proxy network namespace.

Config.Name: Protected networks
Config.Description: Suricata HOME_NET. Use a bracketed comma-separated list of CIDRs.

Config.Name: External networks
Config.Description: Use any behind a reverse proxy so forwarded requests from its internal IP are inspected.

Config.Name: HTTP backend ports
Config.Description: Port group for rules that restrict inspection by HTTP_PORTS. Add your other HTTP backend ports.

Config.Name: Update rules at startup
Config.Description: yes or no. Missing rules are always downloaded.

Config.Name: Daily rule updates
Config.Description: yes or no. Scheduled for 04:17 in the container timezone; see maintenance.log.

Config.Name: Rotate each log at MB
Config.Description: Checked every five minutes, not a strict disk quota.

Config.Name: Rotated copies per log
Config.Description: Number of uncompressed rotated copies per log.
